title: Spring/Summer 2027 Masters AI Training Software & Performance Co-op
description: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. As an AMD co-op , you’ll be placed at the epicenter of the AI ecosystem, working alongside experts and industry pioneers. You’ll do important work, learn new skills, expand your network, and gain real-world experience on projects that impact millions of end-users worldwide. Whether you’re an undergrad or a PhD student, your contributions matter—and your experience here will be a launchpad for what comes next. JOB DETAILS: Location: San Jose, CA, USA Onsite: This role requires the student to work full time ( 40 hours a week), onsite work structure throughout the duration of the co-op/intern term. Duration: Spring/Summer 2027 Co-Op: January 25, 2027 - August 13, 2027 WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING: Would you like to be part of a world-class team enabling software for world-class datacenters and the mightiest supercomputers? AMD is searching for talented and highly motivated AI Software Engineers to join our team of developers pushing the boundaries of efficiency and performance to enable and optimize the software ecosystem for the next generation of GPU computational accelerators. Our team has an unparalleled perspective of the AI landscape. We work with the industry's most sophisticated clients to help them leverage the latest hardware capabilities for their AI use cases. As part of our team, you will be among the first in the world to combine the newest hardware with the industry's latest applications, libraries, frameworks, and SDKs to push the limits of innovation and solve the world's most complex challenges. In this role, you will: Work with a team of software engineers and architects developing AMD Instinct™ GPU AI software. Develop tools for debugging distributed training at a large scale. Analyze and optimize the performance of AI software workloads across training and fine-tuning. Identify hardware and software bottlenecks across CPUs, GPUs, memory systems, and communication infrastructure. Profile and optimize performance across the AI software stack using advanced performance analysis tools. Investigate and develop optimization strategies to improve scalability and efficiency of AI workloads. Implement and optimize parallel computing methods on GPU-accelerated systems. Benchmark, evaluate, and tune AI frameworks, libraries, SDKs, and applications on AMD platforms. Collaborate with architects and engineering teams to drive next-generation AI software performance solutions. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR: Currently enrolled in a master's program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field. Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python with Agentic coding experience. Strong development experience with at least one major deep learning framework such as PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, VLLM, or SGLang Expertise in profiling tools across the AI software stack including PyTorch Profiler, ROCm Profiler, VTune, and Nsight. Experience implementing and optimizing parallel methods on GPU accelerators (NCCL/RCCL, OpenMP, MPI). Advanced performance analysis skills for both CPU and GPU architectures. Deep understanding of latest LLM models and its architectures. Deep understanding of various parallelisms (DP/TP/EP/CP) and their corresponding collectives. Understanding of AI software optimization techniques and performance tuning methodologies. Publications in peer-reviewed AI, Machine Learning, High Performance Computing, or Computer Architecture conferences and journals are a plus. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. title: AI Accelerator Design Verification Engineer Intern
Research Intern - Machine Learning and Optimization - Redmond
description: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Machine Learning and Optimization (MLO) group in MSR-Redmond performs research in the intersection of optimization, machine learning and systems. Our focus right now is in combining ML technology with optimization for efficient decision-making. Example projects include training Large Language Models (LLMs) for algorithm design (e.g., natural language to integer programming, heuristic design), accelerating optimization algorithms for interactive decision dialogues and designing novel algorithms for end-to-end supply chain management. More broadly, our research draws on theoretical insights to design algorithms and machine learning solutions that operate efficiently at scale. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Research Interns are expected to design algorithms/models and prototype them, conduct experiments, and analyze results. They are encouraged to show initiative throughout the research internship and suggest further directions for research. They are expected to document their ideas, and given suitable results, contribute to a paper. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Operations Research or a related STEM field Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications 3+ years of experience in C# or C++ or Python (or similar language) Experience in optimization/algorithm design Experience in machine learning and LLMs (e.g., data curation, post-training, agentic frameworks) Demonstrated ability to run simulations and analyze results The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. title: Process Integration Development Engineer PhD Intern 2027
description: Job Details: Job Description: Work on Intel 14A and explore the engineering challenges behind leading-edge Gate-All-Around (GAA) transistor technology. Join Intel’s Technology Development Foundry Engineering team and contribute to advanced semiconductor process development at the intersection of process integration, device performance, yield, and product execution. As an intern, you will own a focused technical project with practical engineering impact, supported by experienced technical mentors. You will have the opportunity to apply your PhD research expertise to process, metrology, yield, and electrical data and develop insights that can guide engineering decisions. What You Will Work On Depending on your research background, interests, and project needs, your work may include: Analyze inline process, metrology, electrical, and yield data to identify variation, correlations, and opportunities for engineering investigation. Apply statistical analysis, modeling, or data science methods to understand relationships among process conditions, physical measurements, device performance, and yield. Investigate process integration and device-related hypotheses in collaboration with engineers across technical disciplines. Develop automated analysis, standard reports, and visualizations to enable faster assessment of silicon performance and comparison across experiments. Translate analysis into actionable engineering insights and recommendations. Deliver a reusable analysis workflow, reporting tool, or model and present your technical findings to the team. What You Will Gain Hands-on experience supporting Intel 14A technology development. Exposure to how process integration, device performance, yield, and foundry product requirements interact in leading-edge semiconductor development. Experience solving engineering problems using real silicon data. Technical mentorship and collaboration with engineers across multiple specialties. Ownership of a well-defined project with practical engineering value. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications Must be actively pursuing a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Chemistry, or a related scientific/engineering field. Preferred Qualifications PhD research involving advanced semiconductor devices, semiconductor fabrication, or characterization. Hands-on experience with semiconductor fabrication, cleanroom processing, or device/material characterization. Strong data analytics, statistical analysis, modeling, or automation skills. Ability to analyze complex technical data and communicate findings clearly. title: AI for Science Residency - Computational Chemistry
location: Berlin, BE, DE; Cambridge, England, GB; Amsterdam, NH, NL
description: Overview Microsoft Research AI for Science is seeking a postdoctoral researcher in computational chemistry to help generate the data behind Skala, our deep-learning exchange-correlation functional for DFT. You will join a collaborative team of quantum chemists and machine-learning researchers working on data generation for Skala, including the generation of diverse chemical structures. You will work closely with colleagues across data generation, model development and deployment, and you will have access to substantial computational resources. Where possible, results are shared through publications and open-source releases. Contract Length: 2 Years Contract Type: Residency Role Locations: Berlin Germany, Cambridge UK and Amsterdam Netherlands Responsibilities Design, implement and scale methods for generating chemically diverse molecular structures. These include covalent and non-covalent structures (complexes, conformers), bond-dissociation paths and reaction geometries/transition states. Combine and extend structure-generation approaches such as graph-based and fragment-based construction, conformer and reaction-path sampling, and molecular dynamics/metadynamics-based exploration. Use fast approximate methods (e.g. tight-binding) to explore and screen candidate structures. Define sampling and selection strategies so that new data fills gaps in chemical space, and quantify how new structures overlap with existing datasets. Build and maintain robust, automated, reproducible data-generation workflows in Python on shared codebases, working with the team members who run the high-accuracy wavefunction calculations at scale. Work with data-generation, deployment and model-development colleagues to turn evidence from Skala training and benchmarking into priorities for the next datasets. Contribute to the efficiency of the data-generation pipeline, including GPU-accelerated electronic-structure methods where they bring speed-ups. Prepare technical papers, presentations and open-source releases of research code and data. Qualifications Required/Minimum Qualifications: PhD in computational chemistry, theoretical chemistry, computational condensed-matter physics or a related area, completed or close to completion (thesis submitted, or expected within 6 months of the start date), or comparable research experience. Hands-on research experience with electronic-structure methods (DFT and/or semiempirical/tight-binding methods) and with generating, optimising or sampling molecular structures. Proficiency in Python and experience with collaborative code development on shared codebases. At least one peer-reviewed publication or preprint in computational chemistry or a related field. Preferred/Additional Qualifications: Experience developing or contributing to open-source scientific software, for example quantum-chemistry or atomistic-simulation packages. Experience with extended tight-binding (xTB/GFN) methods and with conformer, reaction-path or molecular-dynamics-based structure exploration. Experience building computational-chemistry datasets, for example for training machine-learning models. Experience with GPU-accelerated or high-performance computing for quantum chemistry. Familiarity with wavefunction-based methods (e.g. coupled cluster) and thermochemistry or reaction-energy benchmarks. Experience integrating methods into existing quantum-chemistry codes (e.g. ORCA, PySCF, CP2K) The base pay for this internship is € 8,191.00 per month.
